global.text: With {troop_count} banners now behind me, I trust the council will finally notice who keeps its roads safe.
Ser, {gold} in the coffers and not a single debt to my name. Some of us simply know how to run a treasury.
Took {fief} with {troop_count} men and a sensible plan. Some will call it luck, but I call it planning.
Honestly, I expected more resistance at {fief}. Perhaps the garrison heard my army coming and reconsidered.
My treasury holds {gold} at present. I mention it only so no one can claim I have not earned my seat at the table.
Must be exhausting, ser, watching others count their soldiers while I simply march out and win.
Another week, another win for my banners. I hear the bards are already writing verses about {fief}.
Quite the afternoon at {fief}. Those {troop_count} spears did most of the talking, and I was happy to let them.
Let's be clear: my {gold} stands for prudence, not greed. Anyone who falls short of it may wish to ask me how.
Had the last holder counted their {troop_count} soldiers as carefully as I count mine, {fief} might still be theirs.
The rain over {town} has lasted three days now. I suppose the council will be asked to pay for the mud as well.
Someone please tell the cartographers that {village} is not where their map says it is. I have a delegation to send there.
Lag again this evening. Curious how it always seems worst during the vote on the {town} fief.
A fine night for a stroll along the walls. Strange how the guards never notice a noble slipping in and out of the postern.
Power is much like the weather. Everyone complains of it, nobody can change it, and it always falls on the lowest houses first.
Another week of harvest tallies. I would sooner sit through a tax audit, and that is saying something.
Why did the councillor refuse the ale at {village}? To keep a clear head for the next motion. Ha. Dreadful, I know.
I hear the marshal of {town} has dined with three different lords this month. Useful friends are worth collecting, I find.
The road through {village} is nothing but ruts and ambition. Someone should raise it at council before a cart goes under.
Pleasant evening. Shall we put a motion to council about the bridge repairs at {town}? I have been drafting one for weeks.
Three caravans hit by bandits on the {town} road this week. I raised it at council. Apparently patrols are someone else's budget.
Grain at {town} now costs double what it did last moon. Someone is hoarding, and I have a fairly good idea who profits.
The bandit problem on our roads is not a mystery. It is a question of who got the garrison contracts and who did not.
Bounties are paid out for the same three outlaws every week. Either the bandits are very persistent or the ledgers are very creative.
{rival} was granted the toll roads last council and now complains about bandits on them. Ser, nobody is that unlucky.
Honestly, the siege rules favour whoever shouts loudest at the gate. I would like a vote on it before the next war.
Another week, another lord blaming fate for his ruin. Fate has a name, and it signs its letters at the council.
Ten years of loyal service, and the reward is a tax on salt. I suppose gratitude is not a currency this realm accepts.
Some of us paid our dues to the road wardens and still found our wagons looted near {town}. Perhaps the wardens should be audited.
Ale prices have climbed while tavern quality has fallen. I am not angry, merely disappointed in what our markets have become.
Any house with spare men and a grudge against {enemy_faction}, come to {fief}. Terms are discussed, not dictated.
Rumour says {enemy_faction} has left {fief} thinly garrisoned. Pity nobody has yet thought to ask why.
I am assembling a raid on {fief}. Sensible allies will find me easy to deal with. Foolish ones will find the road long.
Weary of seeing good swords idle. Ser, a siege at {fief} needs hands, and I would rather they be yours than theirs.
Let us be honest: {enemy_faction} will not hold {fief} forever. Join now and history will credit your foresight.
Bring your best cook and your worst temper, Ser. We march on {fief} at dawn.
Ledgers over longswords? A raid on {fief} pays well, and the accounts will be kept honestly. Mostly.
Still no answer from the houses that promised to help at the last assembly. I shall not take it personally. I shall only take notes.
{my_faction} has agreed a campaign against {fief}. Those absent will be asked, politely, which side they were on.
Wars are won by those who arrive first. Our muster is at {fief} at first light. Be there, or be discussed.
Odd how the price of salt in {town} rose the very week the council started asking questions. A coincidence, surely.
Anyone buying iron at {gold} a bar should first ask who profits. I hear certain merchants have friends on the council.
I am told the wool trade in {town} is settling at a fair price. Fair to whom, I wonder, is a question for the next vote.
Ser, if you are haggling, do it quietly. Loud bargains draw attention, and attention draws the council's favour away from you.
I bought grain from {town} for {gold} and found a note asking for my support with it. How very thoughtful of them.
Selling horses at {gold} each is a fine way to earn coin, though I would not trust a buyer who never asks about terms.
Oh, do not mind me. I am only noting that timber prices doubled once a certain lord took the {town} granaries.
Trade is a tool like any other. Those who use it to win allies will outlast those who use it only to win coin.
Whoever wants to sell armour in {town} should come to me first. My buyers pay well and never gossip about their suppliers.
Weary of overpriced ale in every tavern. Perhaps the council should review who sets these prices before the poor go thirsty.
A field battle is only a field battle. The council still counts votes, and {player} has not won one of those yet.
Losing {troop_count} men on the open field is an expensive lesson. I hope the treasury was budgeted for it.
Some win with steel. Others win with signatures. I prefer the second, though I suspect some here will never learn that.
Pity about the banners. Shame they did not hold the ridge long enough to matter to anyone in the chamber.
Enjoy the victory while it lasts, {player}. Councils forget battles quickly, but they never forget who abandoned their allies.
A grand charge, I am told. Shame it will not appear in the next session's minutes.
Every lord hungry for glory eventually learns the field is not where fiefs are decided. Patience, {player}.
{troop_count} soldiers fell today and not one of them was consulted. Remember that the next time you ride out.
I expect the bards will sing of this. I expect the tax collectors will sing louder.
Congratulations on the win. I will be drafting a motion to ensure it does not happen twice.

whisper.text: {player}, a single skirmish changes nothing about the seat I intend to take. Do enjoy your moment.
You won the field and lost the chamber. I wonder which one your creditors will notice first.
A pleasant afternoon for you. I have already noted which of my friends watched it from a safe distance.
Your charge was bold. Your supply lines were not. The council will want a word about that, I assure you.
Keep smiling at the battlefield. I am drafting a letter to the council that will be far less cheerful.
I hope {troop_count} men were worth the glory. Their families will be reading the casualty list soon.
Do not get comfortable. Winning once made you visible, and visibility is a dangerous thing in this realm.
Let me be candid: the victory was noisy and the strategy was thin. Someone should have advised you better.
You have my respect for the charge and my pity for the reckoning that follows. Good day, {player}.
Savour it. I will make sure the next vote reminds you that battles end, but ledgers stay open.

face.text: {player}. You fought well today, I suppose. Pity the council will judge the campaign by its cost, not its courage.
Ah, the victor. Walk with me, and mind the mud. I would hate for you to slip before the next session.
I watched your banners fall back at the ridge and felt the sort of sadness one reserves for a poorly drafted treaty.
You won here, {player}. Remember that fiefs are not held on fields alone. Ask whoever counts the grain stores.
Congratulations. Truly. I shall make certain the council hears every detail, including the parts you would rather forget.
Losing {troop_count} men to take a hillock? Bold. I shall be sure the minutes reflect exactly how bold.
A victory like this makes people nervous, {player}. Nervous people draft motions. You may want to count your friends.
I do not hold grudges over a skirmish. I hold records. Yours is now rather long, and I am very thorough.
Enjoy your ride back to the keep. I will be waiting in the chamber with a list of questions for you.
Some commanders charge. Others count the cost and then vote. I trust you will see which of us is the more useful.

global.text: {player} took the field today. The council will hear the report, and then it will decide what the victory was actually worth.
A battle won, {troop_count} soldiers lost. Accounts will be balanced in the chamber, not on the hill.
Field victories are pleasant, but they do not settle who controls the fiefs. Votes do that, as they always have.
The outcome at the ridge is noted. Now we wait to see what the council makes of it.
Good fighting today. I will reserve judgement until the reports are read, as any sensible member would.
Blood on the grass and ink in the ledger. Both will be counted before the next session, I assure everyone.
I had expected the ridge to fall the other way. Politics is full of such surprises, and this is merely one more.
Someone will need to explain the losses at the ridge. I shall let the council decide who that someone is.
Victory is a fine headline. Governance is the story. I will be watching which one people choose to read.
A clash of banners and a question for the council: was the cost worth the ground? We shall see what the votes say.

whisper.text: {player}, a fair fight by all accounts. I shall be writing my own report for the council before the week is out.
Well fought, I suppose. I am still weighing whether your victory helps or hinders the arrangement I have in mind.
You took the field and I took notes. Let us see which record the council finds more persuasive.
Congratulations on the ridge. Do not mistake a battle for a seat. The two are rarely decided on the same day.
I lost more men than I would have liked. Still, I am inclined to be civil. For now, at least.
Your charge was impressive. I am less sure about the arithmetic afterwards. Shall we discuss it over wine?
I doubt the victory changes much in the chamber. Votes are slow, and people remember the tallies longer than the battles.
Keep your banners flying, {player}. I may need an ally who knows how to win the field, one day soon.
No hard feelings from me. It was a skirmish, not a betrayal. Let us both pretend the matter is closed.
I will not pretend to be pleased, but I am not offended either. The council will sort out the rest in due course.

face.text: {player}. A hard-won field, by the look of your banners. Let us see whether the council considers it hard-won or merely expensive.
You caught me on a poor afternoon, I admit. Tomorrow the ledgers will tell a kinder story, or perhaps a crueller one.
Shall we walk? I would rather talk about the future than the ridge, though the ridge will certainly come up in the chamber.
Well fought, {player}. I suspect we will have more to say to each other once the council has finished its arguments.
A battle is only the first act. The council writes the second, and I have a steady hand with the quill.
I count {troop_count} men lost on my side. Take that number and consider how the council will weigh it against yours.
No need to gloat, {player}. We both know the field is one room in a very large house, and the chamber is another.
Until the next session, then. I will keep my remarks measured, though I cannot promise the same from everyone.
You fought cleanly today. I am curious whether your allies will remember that as fondly as you do.
An honest victory, if a costly one. I shall be watching how you spend it before I decide what to make of you.

global.text: {player} held the ridge like a true champion. The council will hear of it, and I intend to say so myself.
A glorious charge, and a proper lesson for anyone who doubts this coalition. Well done, {player}.
My ally took the field today and came back with the banners. That is what loyal, capable commanders look like here.
The losses at the ridge were heavy, but {player} made them worth it. Let the chamber know who bled for the fief.
Credit where it is due: {player} fought magnificently. I will be pressing the council to reward the effort properly.
{troop_count} soldiers answered the call today. Thanks to {player}, the banners still fly. Remember that at the next vote.
Victory on the hill and a friend on the council. A fine afternoon for our side, all things considered.
Our allies win battles and we win the chamber. Between the two, we make a very strong pair, {player}.
A fine piece of work at the ridge. Shall we make sure the council knows that our coalition stood firm?
The bards will sing of the ridge, and I will make sure the minutes sing along. Splendid work, {player}.

whisper.text: {player}, that charge was magnificent. I will make sure the council hears of it before the week is out.
You carried the ridge and carried my hopes with it. I owe you a favour, and I always pay my debts.
Well done today. Keep your banners close. We have plans for the coming season and you are central to them.
The losses hurt, I know. Do not let them weigh on you. The council will judge the outcome, not the grief.
I was watching from the rear, proud as anything. Shall we draft a letter to the council together?
Your victory strengthens our position considerably. I would like to see you rewarded, and I have a few ideas.
Thank you for holding the ridge, {player}. A commander who wins for our side is one I like to keep close.
Good work today. Let us speak tonight about the seat that will open soon. I have someone in mind, and it is you.
Splendid fighting. I shall be recommending you for the next fief grant, so do keep your reputation polished.
You made us all look capable today. I will not forget it, and I rarely forget the people who help me win votes.

face.text: {player}, what a day. The ridge is ours, and I could not be prouder to stand beside you when the council hears it.
Walk with me, {player}. The victory is only half the story. The other half is who we bring into our circle next.
You fought like someone who understands what is at stake. That is rare, and I intend to make the most of it.
I saw your banners fall and rise again. Such stubbornness wins fiefs in the end, and I intend to say so in the chamber.
Our coalition is stronger for today's work. Shall we sit down this week and plan the next move together?
Lost {troop_count} men, did you? A price worth paying, I think. I will make sure the council knows it was worth it.
A toast later, perhaps? You earned one, and there are a few people I would like you to meet afterwards.
Until the next session, then. Keep your banners high. I will keep my ear to the chamber and my word to you.
You have my thanks, {player}, and I suspect you have the thanks of several other lords who were watching today.
Stay close to our side. The seat I have in mind suits someone who can win fields and keep their friends.

global.text: Another loss to {player}. I begin to suspect the dice are loaded, and the council would do well to ask who holds them.
Three fiefs gone to {player} now. Perhaps the next vote should concern how the realm picks its champions.
I have stopped counting my losses to {player}. The council keeps the tally, and it is not a flattering one for some.
{player} wins again, and I am told this is merit. Curious how merit always arrives with such good timing.
Our banners were beaten at the ford by {player}'s {troop_count} men. I shall be sure the council notes the weather was against us.
Perhaps the realm would be better served if the same name stopped appearing on every field report. Just a thought for the next session.
I will not gloat in public, unlike certain persons. I will simply wait, and the council's memory is longer than any noble's pride.
{player} has beaten us a third time. I dislike admitting it, but I can count, and the numbers are not kind to my side.

whisper.text: {player}, you have bested me thrice now. Do not mistake a lucky season for a lasting one. Seasons turn.
Enjoy the victory, {player}. I have already drafted the motion that will see your next success questioned in council.
Your {troop_count} men were impressive at the crossing. Pity their commander has such a habit of winning at my expense.
I know who has been whispering to the council about my failures. It was not a friend, {player}, and you know it.
Three defeats, {player}. Most would retire quietly. I am weighing a fuss instead, and I rather enjoy that prospect.
You have made an enemy of me, and I am patient. Patience is how the wise take back what the clumsy lose.
Keep winning, {player}. Every victory gives me another line for the minutes, and the council reads those very closely.
I shall not ask how you keep finding the weak point in my lines. I shall simply find who sold you the map.

global.text: {player} has taken another field. Perhaps I should stop reviewing the battle reports and simply read the council's expectations instead.
The council has noted another win for {player}. I make no judgment, though I have watched the same result repeat three times now.
Three losses against the same banner is a pattern, not bad luck. Those who study patterns will see what I see.
Whatever one thinks of {player}'s methods, the results speak clearly enough. I suppose the rest of us must adjust our plans.
A fief changed hands again today. I have no quarrel with the outcome, only with how often it seems to be the same outcome.
Commanders may rise and fall, but the map has a habit of favouring whoever arrives earliest. Some of us are still arriving late.
I congratulate {player} on the latest victory, sincerely, in the way one congratulates weather that has been forecast badly.
Our camp has been quiet since the last fight. Everyone waits to see whether the council changes its mind, or merely its seating.

whisper.text: {player}, the council will want a fair accounting of the last engagement. I trust you have kept your reports in order.
Three times you have bested my side now. I do not say this to wound. I say it because someone should keep the record honest.
I expect the next council session to be lively. Your name will come up, as will mine, and I would prefer we both appear reasonable.
A word of advice: the fief you took was never as valuable as it looked. Ask the people who held it before you.
No hard feelings about the fords, {player}. Perhaps we can speak properly once the council stops measuring everyone's banners.
You are clearly capable, {player}. The question is whether capability is enough to hold what you take, and I have my doubts.
I have no grievance against you personally. The council does, however, and it tends to ask me about you over supper.
If you are open to it, I would welcome an honest conversation about where our interests run together, and where they run apart.

global.text: Third victory for {player} and I find I have run out of excuses. Respect is a strange thing to feel toward a rival, but here we are.
{player} continues to humble our banners, and I must admit the council could not have picked a better opponent to test us.
The realm is better served when its strongest players are measured against one another. {player} has made sure I am measured fairly.
Three losses and I still think {player} is the most interesting person in this war. Stay sharp; I intend to be there when you slip.
Congratulations to {player} on the latest field. I have drafted a motion in your honour, though council will insist on reading it.
It is almost a pleasure to lose to {player}. The fights are clean, the results are plain, and the council respects that sort of honesty.
Credit where it is due: {player} has out-thought us three times now. I would rather have that rival on the field than in the shadows.
I did not expect to be so impressed by a rival who keeps winning. {player} has earned a seat at the table, if the council ever asks.

whisper.text: {player}, I have lost three times to you and somehow still want to buy you a drink. Perhaps we should discuss a truce over supper.
Your {troop_count} men are a credit to whoever trained them. Consider this a formal recognition, offered quietly and in writing.
I will keep my grievances to myself, {player}. A rival who beats me fairly is worth more than an ally who flatters me.
You have beaten me three times, which makes you either very skilled or very lucky. I suspect the former, and I want to hear more.
If you ever need a voice in council, {player}, mine is yours. I have a sense that the council is about to need someone like you.
Losing to you has taught me more about this realm than winning ever did. I do not say that lightly, nor do I expect thanks.
Let us stop trading blows for a season and trade notes instead. I think we would both be surprised at how much we agree on.
Consider this a standing offer, {player}. Should you ever grow tired of winning on your own, my table will always have a chair for you.

global.text: The field belonged to us today. The council will want to know why {player} lost it so quickly.
Another banner fallen to {troop_count} of our men. Some lords should consider their war chests before their pride.
Such a bold charge, {player}. Pity it ended with your troops scattered across the moor. Next council session, perhaps?
Our victory cost {troop_count} soldiers. Yours cost a good deal more, I suspect. I will let the ledgers speak.
I hope {player} enjoyed the field. Tallies for the council are already being written, and your name is on the lower line.
Someone should tell {player} that cavalry does not win battles by itself. Ask any lord who sits on the council.
Strange how quickly {player}'s banners vanished once the real fighting began. Do keep the council informed of your plans.
Our treasurers have priced your captured men at {gold}. Consider it a lesson in what discipline actually costs.
Ask around before your next charge, {player}. The lords who sat through this war are not as forgiving as I am.
A fine morning's work. Your defeat will be read aloud at the next assembly, and I will be sure to read it slowly.

whisper.text: {player}, the field was yours to lose and you lost it. I trust you will explain yourself before the council does.
Do not mistake a skirmish for a verdict, {player}. Still, the seat you hoped to take will be filled by someone sharper.
{troop_count} of your men are now my guests. I suggest you negotiate their return quietly, before the gossip spreads.
Enjoy your retreat, {player}. Eventually someone will need to explain to the council why {gold} was spent for nothing.
I did warn you that recruiting from the wrong fiefs would cost you. Perhaps now you will finally listen to advice.
You fought admirably, {player}, in the way one fights when nobody has counted the numbers beforehand. A pity.
The council rarely forgets a defeat, {player}. I have already made sure a few members heard about this one.
Shall we talk terms, {player}? Your banner is weakened, and my offer will not stay open once the gossip begins.
Next time, {player}, consult someone before you march. Good counsel is far cheaper than {gold} in lost supplies.
Your standard lies in the mud, {player}. I might have it returned to you, for a price and a promise of loyalty.

face.text: {player}. You look like someone who has been counting losses on the road. Be sure to add mine to your list; I was generous with them.
Still hoping for an alliance, {player}? After today I hardly think you are in a position to bargain. Perhaps next season.
I would offer my condolences, but the council already asked me to write the report, and I rather enjoyed writing it.
A soldier's bravery is admirable, {player}. Pity the field rewards arithmetic more than courage. Your numbers were thin.
You will walk the rest of the road with {troop_count} fewer men than you brought. I hope the journey gives you time to reflect.
Do stay a moment, {player}. I want you to hear how the council will describe today before the rumours get ahead of them.
Strange how our banners rallied so quickly. Yours scattered rather fast, did they not? Do think that over on the way home.
Our treasurers have already valued your captured soldiers at {gold}. Consider that a reminder of what you now owe.
I am always glad to meet a rival who learns from defeat. You may yet be useful to me, {player}, if you are quick to learn.
Until the next assembly, {player}. Bring better counsel, or simply bring more troops. Either would be a welcome surprise.

global.text: The field has been decided in our favour. The council will review the battle at its next sitting, as is proper.
Battle reports are circulating. Some lords claim one thing, others another. I prefer to wait for the proper tallies.
{player} fought today with {troop_count} men. Whether that was wise will be a question for the council to settle.
A clash on the eastern road, a victory on our side, and a long list of questions for everyone involved. Typical.
Let the record show the field was contested, the losses were heavy, and the council was not consulted beforehand.
Several lords have asked whether today's result changes the votes. It does not, yet. Patience is a virtue in this chamber.
A battle is only one page of the ledger. The rest will be written in the council chamber, one vote at a time.
Reports of {gold} changing hands after the skirmish are unconfirmed. I would not repeat them until they are verified.
Battles come and go. What matters is who sits in the chamber afterward, and who is still standing at the table.
I have no particular quarrel with anyone who fought today. Only with the paperwork that will follow it.

whisper.text: {player}, the field is done. I have no wish to dwell on it, though the council may think otherwise. Let us speak later.
Nothing personal in today's battle, {player}. Just a result, and a result is something the council will want to discuss.
I noticed your banner held longer than expected. Worth remembering for future votes, I should think.
Your men fought well enough, {player}. The quarrel now is over who writes the account, and I intend to keep the pen.
We are both lords of a sort, {player}, and both answerable to the council. Shall we discuss what today means?
Let us keep our disagreements in the chamber rather than on the moor. The paperwork is far less bloody.
{troop_count} soldiers lost on both sides today. A regrettable sum. I would rather not add to it with pointless feuds.
I hold no grudge over the field, {player}, though I do wonder whose orders carried your troops that far.
Be discreet about today's result for now. The council rewards those who wait for the facts before taking sides.
A draw in spirit, a defeat in the ledger. How you choose to describe it will matter more than the battle itself.

face.text: {player}. A fine field for a skirmish, though I suspect neither of us came for the scenery. Shall we talk about what comes next?
We met on the field, and now we meet on the road. I find that more interesting than the battle, to be honest.
I would not call us enemies, {player}. We are merely parties to an argument the council has not yet settled.
Your troops were quite persistent. Someone should tell you that persistence without support is seldom enough to win.
No hard feelings from my side, {player}. Keep your banner high, and perhaps we will find time to discuss the next vote.
Such a tidy battle for such a messy result. I trust the council will be able to make sense of it by spring.
I am still deciding what to make of today. Ask me again after the next assembly and I may have an answer for you.
Walk carefully on the road, {player}. The lords around here remember who fought hard and who merely stood nearby.
Today was a reminder that the field is cheap and the chamber is expensive. Choose your battles more carefully, {player}.
{player}, I have no interest in prolonging this. Give me a sensible reason to stop, and I shall gladly oblige.

global.text: {player} fought bravely today, and the council should hear about it. Losing the field is no disgrace to a capable commander.
Good fighting today, {player}. Our banner remembers those who stand firm, even when the numbers turn against them.
I would not count today as a defeat for {player}. The council values a capable commander who keeps {troop_count} men together.
Let it be known that {player} held the line longer than most. Such loyalty deserves a seat at the table, not a grave.
Anyone who says {player} lost the field has not seen the wagers on the next council vote. Results will come.
A hard day on the moor, but a worthwhile one. The council will take note of who stayed in the fight.
Friends, do not gossip about the loss. Today's field is a footnote; the next assembly is where it truly counts.
{player} carried the lines well today. We should discuss how that talent might be rewarded when the council meets.
My compliments to {player} for a battle fought with real spirit. Stubbornness like that is rare on the field these days.
Take heart, {player}. A lost battle is only a lost battle, and I have seen worse recovered within a single season.

whisper.text: {player}, you fought well. Do not let the outcome sour you. I have a few friends who would welcome a commander like you.
That was a hard fight, {player}. I spoke well of your stand to the council this evening. Consider it an investment in our friendship.
Your {troop_count} survivors deserve better commanders than the fools who sent them forward. Come speak with me.
Do not sulk over the field, {player}. Losses are useful. They show who is worth recruiting and who is merely loud.
I would like to see you at the next council sitting, {player}. A commander with your spirit could do real good there.
The field was lost, but your reputation is intact, and in my experience that is what the council truly counts.
{gold} would be a fair price to rebuild your company, {player}. I am prepared to discuss terms if you are interested.
Between us, {player}, the defeat was not your fault. The council will hear that from me first, before the gossip does.
You deserve a quieter winter after that battle. Join my circle and I can promise you that much, and more besides.
Keep your chin up, {player}. Good commanders are rarer than good weather, and I have no intention of losing you to idleness.

face.text: {player}, what a battle. You held longer than anyone expected. Come, walk with me. There is much to discuss about the coming season.
I was watching your standard go down, {player}, and I swore to myself I would find you a worthy place in my plans. Shall we talk?
You fought like someone with a future, {player}. Let us not waste it on a single field. Tell me what you need from the council.
A rough day for your banner, but the men who followed you are talking, and I find that promising. Do keep me informed.
Rebuild your ranks and come find me at the next assembly, {player}. I have seats in mind that suit someone of your spirit.
Losing today does not make you smaller, {player}. It only makes the next alliance more valuable to whoever offers it first.
Walk with me, {player}. I want to hear how the field looked from your side, and whether you saw what I saw in the centre.
Your {troop_count} men spoke highly of you as they marched past. That is not something I hear often on this road.
I do not hold the defeat against you, {player}. A council that punished every lost battle would have no lords left to govern.
Until we meet again, {player}. Think about joining our bloc before the summer votes; I would hate to see your talents go to waste.
You may hold my person, {player}, but a captive is not a conquest. The council will hear of this, and its memory is longer than your sword arm.
Enjoy your little victory. Every lord who watched you drag me across that field will remember who chose brute force over a sensible negotiation.
Shall I name the three barons who will cheer my release? Not one of them will mourn your name, {player}. Do try to sleep soundly.
A ransom of {gold} would be a bargain for you and a humiliation for me. Pay it quickly, or I will take my time shaping the story of how you lost my favour.
How very predictable. You took a prisoner to look strong, when you have only proved you lack the patience to win a vote.
Bind my wrists if it comforts you. Bonds are such a clumsy tool, and I have never yet met one I could not talk my way out of.
I am told the hall of {my_faction} still debates whether your banner deserves its place at the table. I fear this little raid will not help your case.
Do not mistake my silence for surrender, {player}. I am merely counting the names of those who will stand at my side when the next session is called.
Well, {player}, you have me. Shall we discuss terms like civilised people, or must we pretend I am simply cargo for the road?
A captive is a curious asset. I am sure you have already weighed what I am worth, though I would advise you to weigh it against what I could tell the council.
Set your demands before the sun moves much further. I have no wish to sit in this cart any longer than necessary, and neither, I suspect, do you.
There are seven fiefs on the western road that have quietly been looking for a new protector. Perhaps we could speak of them instead of ransoms.
I bear you no personal malice, {player}. Politics is simply what happens when two ambitious people share a road and neither trusts the other.
A ransom of {gold} would settle the matter, though I would prefer a discussion first. A written pledge would be cheaper for both of us and far less messy.
You will want witnesses before you act on anything I say. Keep me where the wider assembly can see, and I may find my memory of this day rather generous.
Consider carefully whom you release me to. The wrong hand on my bridle could cost you more than my ransom ever would.
Ah, {player}, of all the banners on that field, I am glad it was yours that caught me. Let us speak plainly, as two people who understand the council's ways.
I shall not pretend this is an unfortunate turn of events. You have always been the sort of ally who knows when to press and when to wait, and I value that.
Keep your guards at ease, {player}. A friend in the hall is worth more to me than any cell, and I intend to repay the kindness when the vote comes round.
Should you wish, I can name the members of the assembly who will owe you a favour after today. I am rather good at remembering who stood by me.
Between us, a ransom of {gold} is a formality. I would far rather see it spent on a seat for you than wasted on some stranger's grudge.
You make a poor brigand and a fine diplomat, {player}. Keep that in mind when the others start counting who backed whom in this affair.
Once I am home, the proposals we discussed will reach the floor quietly. I suspect you will find the other lords more receptive than they were last season.
Do not let the rough road fool you. Your captive remains your admirer, and {my_faction} will recall how generously you treated its representative.
I have read your proposal, {player}, and I have set it beside the other papers that went in the bin this week. The council will not be moved.
No alliance for you, {player}. Go and court someone whose name carries more weight than your last three votes did.
You ask me to stand beside you now? Curious timing, given how often you were seen whispering in {rival}'s hall.
Refused. I will not hitch my banner to someone who cannot keep their own table from spilling. Good day.
Oh, how charming. Another request from you, and I am still waiting for the favour you owed me last session.
I considered it for a moment, {player}. Then I considered what the others would say, and the answer became rather easy.
No. Perhaps when you have won a vote that did not need your cousin to bully it through the room.
Do not mistake my silence for agreement. The answer is no, and I will say so again at the next gathering if anyone asks.
An alliance requires trust, {player}, and trust requires a track record. Bring me one good year and we shall revisit the matter.
I must decline for now. My seat is not yet secure enough to sign anything with a name I have not weighed properly.
Interesting proposal. Unfortunately the timing is poor, and I do not sign pacts in the middle of someone else's quarrel.
Thank you for the offer, but I have already promised my ear to several councils, and none of them favours a new partnership at present.
No, {player}. I keep my options open, and an open hand is not something I hand over after one conversation at the market.
I have heard similar proposals before, usually from people who needed my votes more than I needed their company. Let us see how it develops.
Declined, politely. Should {rival} take an interest in your scheme, I may reconsider, though I would not hold your breath.
I will not commit today. Ask me again after the next assembly, when we all know who is still standing in the hall.
My dear {player}, you flatter me, and I adore being flattered. Still, a formal pact now would only hand my rivals a pretext to meddle.
Not yet, {player}. Let us first pass the grain levy together, and then we can talk about tying our banners more tightly.
I wish I could say yes this very evening. Sadly the council calendar is full, and my allies would never forgive me for rushing.
You know I value you above most of the hall. That is precisely why I am not ready to bind us in writing before the spring vote.
Splendid thinking, truly. Keep bringing me ideas like this and I shall find the right moment to make the arrangement official.
Ah, {player}, I am sorry. My hands are tied by a promise to a faction that would not look kindly on a new partner just now.
Let us keep this between friends for the time being. A quiet understanding serves us both better than a loud contract that everyone reads.
No formal alliance today, but do keep me informed of your moves. I will be quietly cheering from the gallery when they succeed.
Very well, {player}. I shall accept your alliance, though I expect the council to hear of it before the week is out, and I will not be the one who explains why.
An alliance, then. How convenient. Lords who come asking for favours are often the first to forget them, so I shall keep a careful ledger.
I accept. Let us put the terms in writing so that no one, least of all {rival}, can later claim we agreed to something we did not.
Agreed. Mark that I was the one who extended the hand first, should the minutes ever be read aloud at the next assembly.
Fine. Your banners may fly beside mine for now, though I have seen many such arrangements dissolve once the harvest taxes fall due.
I shall accept, {player}. Do not mistake courtesy for trust. I simply prefer to keep my rivals where I can see them.
Very well. I will bring the proposal before the council tomorrow, where I am certain a few members will ask questions you may not enjoy answering.
Accepted. I am sure {rival} will be delighted to hear of it, or will at least pretend to be, which at court amounts to much the same thing.
Gladly, {player}! Together our fiefs could outvote everyone who has been sneering at us in the great hall, and I do enjoy the thought of that.
You have made a sensible choice, and I would hate for you to regret it. Let us draft the charter before someone else thinks of the idea.
I accept with real pleasure. Between the two of us, the council seats will fall to people who actually understand how this realm works.
Splendid. I had hoped you would come to me first, and I shall tell the others the idea was mine from the start, naturally.
Yes, yes, a thousand times yes. Bring your envoys to supper and we will sort out who gets which fief over a very good bottle of wine.
Agreed, and happily so. With you at my side, {rival} will find it much harder to explain away the failed grain levy in front of the assembly.
I accept, {player}. You have a sharp mind for these matters, and I suspect we will recruit a few more allies before the next vote.
A wise decision, and one I shall be sure to mention when the next council seat is discussed. Shall we say the bell tower at dusk?
I shall remember this little exchange when the council next sits, {player}. Memory is a patient sort of weapon, you know.
Go on, then. Walk away. The rest of the realm will be talking about who blinked first, and I do hope it is not you.
We are finished here, and I suspect the fief will be better governed for it. Try not to trip over your own ambitions on the road.
Mind the bridge at the ford, {player}. It has a habit of collapsing under people who stand too near to my dealings.
A pleasure as always, which is to say not at all. I will draft the minutes of this meeting myself, so you may rest assured of their accuracy.
Good day. I have three letters to write before supper, and at least one of them will concern you and the company you keep.
Off you go. When the vote comes, I expect your absence will be noticed far more than your presence ever was.
Farewell, {player}. Do not bother sending word of the next council. I have already told the others what to expect from you.
I think we both know this will not end well for one of us, and I have already made my choice of which one. Good day.
Very well. We shall speak again when there is something worth the time, though I am not yet convinced there will be.
Thank you for your company this afternoon. I will weigh what you said against what others have told me, and then decide what it meant.
Until we meet at the council, I suggest you consider which side of the table you would prefer to sit on. The seating is not yet fixed.
Good day to you. Mind the carts on the east road; they have been blocking traffic since the harvest levies were announced.
We have covered a good deal of ground today. I shall see what the fief elders make of it before I commit to anything further.
Farewell for now. I expect a number of rumours will reach you before sundown, and I would be grateful if you judged them on their merits.
This has been a useful conversation, if not a conclusive one. Let us reconvene once the tithe reports have been read and properly argued over.
Take care on the road. Plenty of people are asking questions about the grain stores this week, and I should hate for you to be caught unawares.
Well, that was civil enough. I will consider your proposal alongside the others on my desk, which is a longer list than you might imagine.
I have other appointments, I am afraid. But do give my regards to whoever it is you are answering to these days, for I have been wondering.
Ah, {player}, you have made my day considerably brighter. We must dine properly soon and perhaps draft something together for the council.
Safe travels, my friend. Keep your ears open in the market; I am certain you will hear something useful for both of us.
Off to the western fiefs, then? Send word of any movements there, and I shall return the favour with everything I learn.
Go with my blessing, though I confess my blessing is always conditional on your continued enthusiasm for our little arrangement.
You are one of the few who truly understands how these things are done. Let us speak again before the next vote, and bring your best ideas.
Another splendid meeting. I shall write to the others tonight and tell them you are the sort of ally they ought to have counted on sooner.
Walk well. Should anyone ask your opinion of me, I trust you will remember that I have been nothing but generous to your interests.
Off you go, then. I have a few quiet words to arrange on your behalf, and I rather enjoy being the one who makes things happen.
It is always a pleasure to speak with someone who sees the realm's future as clearly as you do. Let us keep this partnership quietly in mind.
Farewell, dear friend. Remember that a well-placed favour today is worth a dozen speeches in the council hall next season.
Ah, {player}. I had hoped the road would bring me someone sensible, yet here you are, blocking the path as though the realm owed you a toll.
I shall not waste my breath pretending to be pleased. Whatever you intend to propose at the next council, I have already read the minutes of your last failure.
Step aside, {player}. {my_faction} has business in these hills, and I would rather not spend the afternoon explaining to the marshals why you were trampled.
You will forgive me if I do not offer a hand. The last time we shared a table, the wine was poor and your promises were poorer still.
Pleasant as always, {player}, though I notice the smile never reaches the eyes. A pity. It would have made the next vote so much easier to count.
Let us be brief. {my_faction} does not require your company, your coin, or your opinions on how the granary should be run.
Every road in this valley seems to lead to your ambitions, {player}. I would prefer you found a different road, one that leads somewhere far from my lands.
Mark me well: when the council sits again, I will be sitting across from you, and I intend to enjoy watching you explain yourself.
Do not mistake my silence for surrender. I merely remember faces, {player}, and yours has been placed firmly in the column of debts I mean to collect.
Good day, {player}. We cross paths often enough that I have stopped asking where you are going, though I confess I still wonder why you never choose a shorter road.
{persona} of {my_faction}, at your service, for whatever the service is worth. Shall we exchange pleasantries, or simply agree to keep our banners apart?
I have no quarrel with you today, {player}. Let us keep it that way, and perhaps the council will be spared another afternoon of tedious speeches.
Ah, a traveller. Forgive me if I keep my hand near my purse, {player}; I have learned that every courteous greeting in this province arrives with a bill attached.
We are not friends, and we are not enemies, which I find to be the most useful position a seat at the council can hold. I trust you find it equally convenient.
Your name has reached my ears a few times this season, {player}, usually in the company of people I would rather not discuss over supper. Pass on my regards to them, if you must.
Shall we pretend this meeting is accidental? It saves us both the trouble of explaining why {my_faction} and your household happen to be heading toward the same market.
I will be frank, since frankness costs less than flattery. I do not yet know whether you are useful to me, {player}, and until I do, you will remain a pleasant face on a dusty road.
Good weather for travel, is it not? I have been told the harvest councils begin soon, and I expect you will have a great deal to say when they do.
You may continue on your way, {player}. I shall watch where your banners go, purely out of civic duty, of course, and not because I am curious.
{player}! What a joy to meet you here. Stay a while, for I have been eager to hear your thoughts on the new charter before the others get to them.
There you are, {player}. I was just telling my steward that the best thing about this season is the company of people who think as clearly as you do about the realm.
Splendid timing. I had intended to send word to you this evening, and now I can save the messenger's fee and make the offer in person.
Our two houses have so much to gain from one another, {player}. Let us not waste a fine afternoon on the road when we could be drafting the terms over a proper meal.
I trust you are well? You look every bit the figure who will carry the next vote, and I should like to be standing at your side when it is counted.
{persona} of {my_faction} greets you warmly. Should you wish to bring your people into our fold, I can promise them a seat at the table and a voice that will be heard.
It is always a pleasure to see your banner, {player}. The council grows duller in your absence, and I am quite certain the gossips miss you as well.
Come, let us speak candidly. I have heard whispers that your fief is restless, and I believe a modest alliance could settle matters to everyone's advantage.
Ah, {player}, the one face on this road I was glad to see. Send word of any plans you make, and I shall ensure they reach the right ears.
Safe travels, then. Write when the council sits, and perhaps we can arrange our votes so that certain people are left rather embarrassed in the chamber.
Ser {player}, a demand delivered at swordpoint is hardly a negotiation. I shall make certain the council hears exactly how you chose to conduct yourself today.
Surrender, you say, and hand over {gold} besides? How bold of you. I have already drafted the motion that will see your ambitions sit on a very small bench.
I have sat through worse threats from men with far larger armies than yours, Ser {player}. Forgive me if I do not tremble at a single raised voice.
Keep your {gold} in your coffers. Every coin you extract from me will be recorded, and every one will be used against you when the next vote is called.
How tiresome. You arrive with threats and no witnesses, then expect me to reward the performance. Perhaps the council would find your methods as amusing as I do not.
Pay {gold} to someone who cannot even hold a civil tongue? I would sooner watch the grain rot in my own storehouses, and I suspect many others would agree.
Threats are the last refuge of those who have lost the debate. Do continue, Ser {player}. Every word you speak today is one more line in the minutes.
Very well. I will bring this to the council, and you may explain to them why a fief-holder's first resort is extortion dressed up as diplomacy.
Consider this my answer: no gold, no surrender, and a quiet promise that your name will be remembered at the next gathering, though not fondly.
I was going to be gracious. You have made that rather difficult, Ser {player}, so enjoy whatever small satisfaction threatening me brings you this afternoon.
Ser {player}, you have made your demand clear enough. Now let us see whether it survives a proper hearing before the council, where such matters are usually settled.
Surrender or pay {gold}? Those are rather stark terms for a first meeting. I would prefer to hear what lies behind them before I decide anything at all.
I note your demand and your tone. Whether either will hold up to scrutiny is another matter, and a fair few of my colleagues will want to weigh in on it.
A threat, followed by a price. It is a familiar pattern in these parts. Perhaps we can skip the middle step and speak plainly about what each of us stands to gain.
Parting with {gold} is never a small matter, Ser {player}. Put your claim in writing, and I will have it read before the council at the next sitting.
You may be right that the roads are dangerous these days. Still, I would rather not decide the fate of my coffers while standing in a muddy field.
Let us be sensible. Threats make for poor minutes, and the council keeps very careful minutes. Name the terms you truly want and we can see what is possible.
I am not in the habit of surrendering anything on a single afternoon's notice. Send word through the proper channels and we shall consider your demand properly.
Interesting. Most who arrive with demands like yours already have someone waiting in the wings. Whose advice did you take before coming to me today?
Your demand has been noted, Ser {player}. I will weigh it against the other matters on my desk, and I expect the answer will be a good deal less dramatic than you hoped.
Ser {player}, you know I value you far too much to let a little misunderstanding turn into a feud. Let us talk it over, and perhaps {gold} can be framed as a gesture of goodwill.
Surrender is such a harsh word between friends. Call it a contribution to the common good instead, and I will be the first to speak for you at the council.
I confess the demand stung a little, Ser {player}. Still, I know you rarely make such a move without good reason, so let us find a solution that flatters us both.
Ha! You always did enjoy a dramatic entrance. Come, let us sit somewhere quieter and discuss how {gold} might serve both our interests before the gossips start talking.
Between us, a demand like that will only make certain people wonder who truly holds influence in this region. I would rather the wrong people did not get ideas.
Your friendship means more to me than a purse of {gold}, so do not think I refuse lightly. I merely wish to see the arrangement made in a way the council will admire.
Dear Ser {player}, I have never once regretted standing by you. Let us keep it that way, and I will see that the matter is handled quietly and to your benefit.
Very well, you have my ear. Give me a day to speak with the right people, and I shall return with terms that protect your standing rather than embarrass it.
Hard bargains are the currency of this realm, and you have always been fair in your dealings with me. Let us be practical, shall we, and see what can be arranged.
Ser {player}, I am glad you came to me instead of the others. Keep me informed of your plans, and I will ensure your name is spoken kindly when the next vote is called.
Your offer of {gold} is generous, {player}, though I do wonder what the council will say when they learn who truly profits from it. I shall raise it at the next vote.
A trade with you, {player}? I recall the last one left {town} short of grain and me short of patience. I will weigh this one very carefully indeed.
Bring your {gold} to the council hall and we shall see whether your terms survive daylight. Most of my colleagues have long memories for such things.
How thoughtful of you to propose a deal now, after the fiasco at {town}. I shall consider it, though my answer will be no, and I shall explain why at length.
Decline? Oh, I could never be so blunt. I shall simply forward your proposal to the faction and let its members find the flaws you so carefully hid.
Your {gold} is tempting, {player}, but I have learned that people who rush to buy my favour often want something I cannot afford to give away.
I will think on your proposal. Do not mistake the time for hesitation; it is the courtesy I extend to those whose reputations I have yet to fully examine.
Ah, another deal from {player}. Pray tell, which of my allies did you already court before coming to me? Such inquiries have a way of reaching the council.
Terms are terms, {player}. Put your proposal in writing, name the fief involved and the {gold} changing hands, and I shall bring it before the next session.
A trade of {gold} for passage through {town}? Interesting. Who else sits on your side of this arrangement, and what do they stand to gain?
I am not opposed to commerce. I am, however, opposed to being surprised by it. Explain yourself fully and I will decide whether the council needs to hear of it.
Your offer is noted. Give me a week to consult those who matter, and do not be offended if their reply arrives before yours does.
Perhaps. Trade has a way of making friends and enemies in equal measure, and I have yet to decide which camp this proposal belongs in.
Let us speak plainly about the {gold} on the table. I would prefer a deal that the whole hall can see, rather than one whispered behind closed doors.
Very well, {player}, I shall listen. Though I have heard many promising proposals from this quarter, and not all of them survived the first vote.
There may be merit in this arrangement. Before I commit, I should like to know how the terms affect {town} and the lords who have the most to lose.
Splendid, {player}! I knew you would see the advantage. Shall we seal the {gold} agreement before the council meets, so that no one can claim they were not consulted?
Your proposal is exactly the sort of initiative this realm needs. Come, let us draft the terms over wine, and I will bring two allies to lend weight to it.
Ah, a deal worthy of our partnership. I will gladly champion it, though I expect you to remember who stood beside you when the votes were counted.
Accepted in principle, my friend. Put the {gold} figure in writing and I will ensure the rest of the hall hears only praise for the arrangement.
You have a talent for proposals that suit everyone at this table, {player}. Pray tell, who else have you brought into this? I would like to make certain they are ours.
A fine offer. I will confess that I had hoped you would come to me first, and I would be delighted if you would join my faction when we speak of {town}.
This is how alliances are built, one honest bargain at a time. Let us meet again soon, and bring your ideas for {town}; I have a seat in mind for you.
Yes, yes, I accept! Think how this strengthens us both before the rivals catch wind of it. We shall have the whole council talking of our success by week's end.

global.text: The field at {enemy_faction}'s border was won today. The council will sort out who deserves the credit. It always does.
{troop_count} troops took that ridge. I counted, and then I counted again. The minutes will reflect this, naturally.
A fine victory. Pity the campaign ledger still has blank columns where the names of the commanders should be.
Victories are easy to announce. Votes on who shares the spoils are where things get interesting.
Good work on the field today. Let us see whether it survives a session of the council before the wine runs out.
A battle won with {troop_count} blades is a debt owed by someone. I shall be keeping a careful tally.
The banners flew for our side today. Whether they fly tomorrow depends on who speaks loudest in the hall.
{enemy_faction} lost a field today. I will leave it to the scribes to decide who earned the glory.

whisper.text: {player}, that flank held better than expected. I shall note it, though I note most things.
A useful day in the field. I trust our arrangement remains a matter of convenience, as it was before.
We fought well together. Do not mistake a shared battle for a shared future, {player}.
I saw you hold the line with {troop_count} men. Impressive. I wonder what you will ask for in return.
Our banners were on the same side today. The council will decide whether that means anything tomorrow.
Well fought, {player}. I shall bring your conduct to the next vote, favourably or otherwise.
Do not read too much into today. Allies are useful until the next grant of land is on the table.
A good day's work. I will be writing to the council about it, and I will mention you only in passing.

face.text: {player}. A fine fight today. I shall reserve judgement on whether it changes anything between us.
Ah, {player}. We held the field together. Now the real contest begins, in the council chamber.
You fought at my side and I am still deciding whether that was a kindness or a calculation. Good day.
Tell me, {player}, what did you gain from today? I always ask, and I always listen to the answer.
Our {troop_count} did well enough. Let us speak again when the vote on the spoils is called.
Walk with me a moment. The victory was ours, but the question of who holds the fief is still open.
Good work, {player}. I have seen many a fine battle end in quiet bickering over who led the charge.
We stood together today. Keep your eyes open, though. Shared banners do not always stay shared.

global.text: {player} held the eastern road today. Their name will be mentioned in council, and I shall make sure of it.
Our thanks to {player} and every soldier who stood with them. The council does not forget loyal service.
Few lords hold a line the way {player} did today. I intend to say so in the hall, and loudly.
Victory against {enemy_faction}, with {player} at the centre of it. A fine example for the rest of us.
I have already drafted a motion honouring {player}. Let the hall argue about it; the result is clear.
{troop_count} strong, and led with sense. {player} has earned a seat at any table I control.
Today's win belongs to all who fought, but {player} deserves a larger share of the praise.
Someone should raise a toast to {player}. I will raise the motion before the wine is poured.

whisper.text: {player}, that charge was magnificent. I will push for a fief grant in your name at the next session.
You fought beautifully today. I trust you remember who spoke for you when the votes were counted.
Keep this up and I may have to start calling you an ally in front of the whole council, {player}.
Between us, your stand at the ford was the reason we won. I intend to see that it is recorded properly.
I have a seat that could use someone of your judgement. We can discuss it over dinner, if you are free.
The council will hear of your courage, {player}. And I will hear whether you are still willing to work with me.
Your {troop_count} made the difference today. Let us talk about how that difference might be rewarded.
A fine day, {player}. Let us make sure the next council sitting is just as fruitful for us both.

face.text: {player}! That charge was splendid. Walk with me; there is a motion I want to put before the council.
I was hoping we would meet. Your stand today has given me ideas about the future of our alliance.
Do you know how rare it is to find an ally who fights well and also knows how to speak in the hall? Rarer still.
Well done, {player}. Once the dust settles, I would like to hear what you want from the next vote.
You fought well, and I intend to mention it at every opportunity. Consider it a down payment, not a favour.
Keep your banner high, {player}. The council seats are shifting, and I would like you in a good one.
Our {troop_count} carried the field. Shall we discuss what that means for the fiefs next season?
A pleasure to stand beside you today. Our shared banner looks better with you under it.

global.text: The council votes on Tuesday, and I'd hate for anyone to miss the chance to explain why {fief} is now in better hands.
Ha! {enemy_faction} left their gates unguarded and we simply walked in. Strategy is a wonderful thing, isn't it?
Lords of Ormerath, take note: {my_faction} holds {fief} now, and we intend to govern it far better than its last keepers.
Oh, do forgive the tears in {enemy_faction}'s banners. I'm sure they'll find another flag to wave soon enough.
Some lords rule by sword, others by patience. I'd like to think {my_faction} managed both at {fief}.
The garrison at {fief} surrendered after a single afternoon. I'm told their morale was more fragile than their walls.
Let it be recorded that {my_faction} took {fief} through proper channels. The council will be pleased with the paperwork.
Pity about {enemy_faction}. Surely someone should have told them that castles need more than good intentions to hold.
The truce with {faction} was signed in the council hall, not on a battlefield. That is how civilised lords settle matters.
I did warn that the war was costing us more than any reward could repay. Peace with {faction} is a relief, if a late one.
{my_faction} has made terms with {faction}. Let no one claim we did not weigh every harm before accepting.
Some will mourn the battles we did not win. I mourn the coin we wasted on them, and I shall say so at the next sitting.
The next vote in council should prove far livelier than any siege. I have already drafted my remarks.
Who drafted the clauses with {faction}? The answer is in the minutes, for anyone who cares to read them.
Ser, I hear the taverns are calling this a defeat. Curious, since {faction} now owes us a favour in writing.
Blood is spent and the treaty with {faction} is only ink now. Ink, I find, outlasts grudges by a wide margin.
Laying siege to {fief} is bold, {player}. Pity the council will be asked to pay for the damage before the walls even fall.
Some who lay siege mistake it for a conquest. {fief} has walls, and the council has memories of who broke them last time.
Ser {player} has discovered that banners are cheap and stone is not. The council will be pleased to tally the cost.
Setting up camp outside {fief} is a fine way to gather attention. A shame attention is all it will earn.
The council will convene on the siege of {fief} at dusk. Let it be recorded who chose to start it without a vote.
I trust {player} has considered the upkeep on siege engines. Ours are paid for by taxes, which the council debates.
Strange how eager some are to fight for a fief they have never governed. Ambition makes poor masonry, I find.
Every siege ends in a negotiation. I merely wonder whether {player} will be the one asking for terms or granting them.

whisper.text: {player}, lifting your siege of {fief} now would save us both an embarrassing council session. Consider it a courtesy.
You have chosen a poor moment, {player}. Half the banners at {fief} are reconsidering their loyalty as we speak.
A siege is a loud way to announce a grievance. Quieter channels exist, and I would gladly show you one.
Your men will tire long before the walls do, {player}. Withdraw, and we can discuss this like reasonable parties.
Do give my regards to whoever approved that siege. I am curious how they plan to feed the garrison at {fief}.
Gates inside {fief} have a way of opening for the right voices, {player}. Pause, and let us talk.
Every siege needs a supply road, {player}. I have already had mine closed, and I suspect yours is next.
Turn back from {fief} while there is still a face to save, {player}. The council rarely forgives a fool twice.

global.text: {player} has moved against {fief}. The council will want a formal account before anyone takes sides.
A siege at {fief} raises the question of who authorized it. I am sure the minutes will be thorough.
Bold move on {fief}. Let us see whether the banners hold longer than the goodwill did.
News of the siege at {fief} is spreading. Some will call it ambition, others will call it a tax problem.
No one has yet explained what {player} hopes to gain at {fief}. I am interested in the answer, not the banners.
Watching {fief} come under siege is never pleasant. I would rather see the matter settled at the table.
The garrison at {fief} is loyal, for now. Loyalty tends to shift when the supply carts stop arriving.
A siege of {fief} changes the map for everyone, not only those holding it. Plan accordingly, friends.

whisper.text: {player}, I see you have begun at {fief}. Before the wagons arrive, let us discuss what the council will accept.
Your siege is noted, {player}. I have no objection yet, though I reserve the right to form one by morning.
I hope you have a reason for {fief} that will survive a vote. Mere ambition rarely does, in my experience.
Should you need a neutral voice at the council regarding {fief}, I am willing to speak. For a modest consideration.
No hard feelings about {fief}, {player}. Politics is politics, and the seat will be filled by someone eventually.
The garrison at {fief} is asking questions, {player}. Answer them well, and I may stay out of this entirely.
I suppose the siege of {fief} is a statement. I would prefer we meet first and make it an agreement instead.
Keep your banners where they are for now, {player}. I will hear your side before I decide what mine should say.

global.text: Losing {troop_count} men in one afternoon is a feat. Most would have the decency to stay quiet about it.
The council will hear every detail of that rout. I have already drafted the minutes, and they are not kind.
Funny how an army of {troop_count} can vanish while the banners stay so proudly raised.
Some commanders learn from defeat. Others simply call another vote and declare the outcome a victory.
Ser {player} has discovered a new way to lose a battle. Pity it cannot be recorded as a lesson.
A pity about the {troop_count} soldiers. They will be remembered at the next assembly, if only as a footnote.
Those who lead from the back should not be surprised when the front line breaks. Ask anyone who was there.
Do not mistake a retreat for strategy, whatever the herald says. The fief has noticed, and so have I.

whisper.text: {player}, {troop_count} dead men will make a poor argument at the next vote. I would start preparing excuses now.
I heard about the rout. Such a shame. Perhaps the council will finally ask who truly planned that march.
Do not expect sympathy from me. I warned your camp about that ridge, and you chose pride instead.
The seat you hoped to keep is already being measured by others. Consider this a courtesy, {player}.
{troop_count} soldiers, gone. I suppose someone will have to answer for the arithmetic, and it will not be me.
Feel free to blame the weather. Everyone else will blame your judgement, and they have far better memories.
If you need a friendly ear while your reputation bleeds, you know where I keep my patience. It is limited.
You will need allies after this, {player}. I suggest you stop making enemies in the same breath as losses.

global.text: A bad day for {player}, and a worse one for the {troop_count} who followed orders. The council will sort out the blame.
Reports of the defeat are spreading faster than the surviving soldiers. Curious how stories travel.
Losing most of one's army is hardly the end of a campaign. It is merely the start of a long audit.
{troop_count} troops withdrawn from the field. Whether that counts as strategy depends on who writes the record.
Some will call it a rout. Others will call it a lesson in humility. Both readings will be argued at length.
The fief has seen worse days. Whether {player} recovers is a question for the next assembly.
Morale is fragile after a loss like that. I expect the coming weeks will show who holds their nerve.
Defeat is never final on Ormerath, only expensive. Let us see what {player} can afford to rebuild.

whisper.text: {player}, I am sorry about the battle. Rebuilding {troop_count} men is slow work, but not impossible.
I have read the reports from the ridge. The details are unflattering, though not all of them are your fault.
Should you need counsel on rebuilding, I am willing to listen. Nothing comes free in these halls, however.
The council will want a reckoning. Before they ask, it might help to decide what you intend to say.
Losing that many soldiers changes the balance of every alliance you hold. Consider who now needs you more.
I will keep my opinions to myself for the moment. Once the dust settles, we can talk plainly.
Defeat stings, {player}. Do not let it persuade you to make rash promises to people who will forget them.
A rout is only a rout until the next council sits. After that it becomes a story, and stories can be rewritten.

global.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the ridge, and still held the line longer than most would. Respect is due.
Let the gossips gossip. A commander who survives a rout with the banner intact is worth backing.
Hard fortune struck {player} today. The council should remember who fought hardest before the collapse.
We lost ground and blood at the ridge, but not our honour. That counts for something in this realm.
A bruising defeat, and yet {player} is still standing. I will say so in the hall, and I will mean it.
Rebuild quickly, {player}. Our fief needs a commander who learns from a loss rather than hiding from it.
The {troop_count} who fell will be honoured in council. Their sacrifice is not wasted on those who listen.
Do not let the chatter bring you down. Defeats make good leaders, provided their allies stay loyal.

whisper.text: {player}, that was a brutal afternoon. I am sorry for the losses. Come and talk when you are ready to plan.
I saw what you tried at the ridge. Bad luck, nothing more. We can turn {troop_count} lost men into leverage.
Ser {player}, the council respects a commander who keeps their nerve. Let us make sure they remember that.
Between us, the vote can wait. Rest first, then we will discuss who should be seen to share the blame.
I have already spoken for you in the hall. Do not thank me yet, as favours here always carry interest.
You know I will back you. A few well-placed words and this defeat becomes a story about perseverance.
Losing {troop_count} soldiers is painful, but your allies are still here. That matters more than the ridge.
Keep your head high, {player}. The rivals who are smiling today will be asking for favours by the new moon.

global.text: {player} ran from my banners before a single arrow flew. Bold strategy, if the goal was to be seen running.
Withdrawing from the field keeps one's standing intact, or so I'm told. Pity the standing of the fleeing party now looks rather thin.
The council debates courage at length. {player} has settled the question for us, and quite decisively.
Forty riders vanished over the ridge at first sight of our pennants. I wonder what the grain-fief stewards will make of that.
Shall we record {player}'s retreat in the minutes as a tactical withdrawal? I'm sure the clerks would find it generous.
Some lords lead from the front. Others lead from the next county over, and {player} has clearly chosen the latter.
A fine turn of speed from {player} today. Shame the speed was not matched by any intention of holding the road.
Pennants scattered, ledgers lost, and {player} halfway to safety. The assembly will want an explanation, and I have drafted several.
Running was sensible, I grant you. Less sensible is announcing the retreat to half the realm before the dust has settled.
Another day, another flight from {player}. At this rate the field might be declared a permanent vacancy.

whisper.text: {player}, you ran before the arrows flew. Think carefully about who will remember that when the next seat falls open.
Your retreat was noticed by every banner on the ridge. I trust you have a speech prepared for the next assembly.
One who flees at first sight of banners makes a poor ally. I'm sure you knew that already.
Enjoy the road home, {player}. My scouts will keep watch, and so will my friends on the council.
Shall I take your silence as agreement that the fief was never really yours to defend?
That was not a retreat, {player}. It was an audition for a role someone else will be happy to fill.
You might consider a more accommodating attitude toward the council. Fleeing battles is a habit the assembly dislikes.
Running from my party cost you more than a skirmish. Several votes I could name will now go elsewhere.
I have no wish to be unpleasant, {player}. But a flight like that is hard to forgive when others are fighting.
Next time, at least have the courtesy to scatter with some dignity. The grain-sellers talk, you know.

global.text: {player} pulled out before the first clash. Make of that what you will; I have already made my own notes.
Some ran, some stood. I'm keeping an open mind about which group deserves a seat at the table.
The retreat from the ridge has people asking questions. Nobody has yet asked the right ones, which is convenient.
Tactics are a matter for the war council, not the hedgerows. {player} seems to have decided to lead from the hedgerows.
A quiet withdrawal today may be a wise one tomorrow. The council will judge once the reports are complete.
Riders from the western muster brought word of {player}'s departure. Accounts differ on whether it was strategy or panic.
Let us not rush to judgment over one skirmish. Reports are still being drafted, and drafts have a way of changing.
Withdrawing before contact is respectable when the numbers look wrong. Whether they were wrong is still debated.
I suppose {player} had reasons. The assembly will ask for them, and they will be politely hard to refuse.
Seats are not lost in a single afternoon. They are lost gradually, one retreat at a time, as the minutes pile up.

whisper.text: {player}, I saw you withdraw from the ridge. No need to explain now, though I may ask for an explanation later.
A retreat before the first clash can be sensible, or it can be a signal. I am still deciding which this was.
Keep your options open, {player}. Today's withdrawal is a small matter, and small matters have a way of growing.
I'd rather hear your side before the council hears theirs. Send a note when you have the time.
You turned your party around before contact. Tell me the reasoning sometime; I find it more interesting than the battle.
The field went badly for everyone who stayed. Those who left have some explaining to do, yourself among them.
Let us speak once the dust settles. Votes are easier to count when everyone has calmed down.
You are welcome to a seat at the next assembly regardless of today. Just do not make me regret saying so.
I noticed the withdrawal. I also noticed nobody else in your party looked surprised by it, which says something.
Consider this a neutral observation, {player}. The council keeps records, and today's record is still unwritten.

global.text: {player} withdrew from the ridge with admirable discipline. A tactical retreat, and a sensible one, I'd say.
Nobody sensible stands alone against a field of banners. {player} knows that, which is why I rate their judgment highly.
The council heard how {player} pulled the party clear. Several members have already asked who to thank for the advice.
Our friends who saw the retreat are saying it was wise. I have been saying so since the first horn sounded.
Living to fight another day is hardly cowardice. Ask anyone who has sat through a long assembly and still won the vote.
{player} kept the party intact today, which matters more than a single skirmish. Remember who was on the road with you.
A fine piece of judgment from {player}. The assembly may not appreciate it yet, but it will.
Today's withdrawal was prudent, and I intend to make sure the minutes say so clearly and at length.
{player} saw the odds and acted on them. That kind of clear sight is rare, and the council should be grateful for it.
Good to see {player} still in the saddle after that tangle. A stronger faction needs people who know when to step back.

whisper.text: {player}, that was well judged. Pull back now, regroup, and I will make sure the council hears how sensibly you acted.
You made the right call on the ridge. I'll speak for you at the next assembly, and you can return the favour when a seat opens.
Your party is intact because you read the field correctly. That is a quality I would like to see more of in our ranks.
Nicely handled, {player}. Keep your people close and your messages closer; I have a few names I want you to meet.
Good retreat. I was worried for a moment, but I should have known you would not walk into a bad fight.
If anyone asks, you were never running. You were preserving the faction's strength for the vote that actually matters.
Come by my hall when you are settled. There are two fiefs and one council seat I would like your view on.
The field went to the other side, but you kept your riders alive. Think of that as the first step in a longer game.
I'll say it plainly: you keep better judgment than most who sit at the table. Do not let one bad afternoon change that.
Rest your horses, {player}. We have a meeting to prepare, and I would like you beside me when it begins.

global.text: Funny how a fief lands in {player}'s lap the same week the council stopped asking my opinion. Coincidence, surely.
A castle for {player}? The council must be short on members who actually read the ledgers.
Let us all applaud {player}, who discovered that {fief} comes with a seat at the table. Remarkable timing.
