Grants are only as good as the votes behind them. I wonder how many members were consulted on {fief}.
{fief} changing hands again. I do hope its new keeper enjoys the upkeep bills. Nobody mentions those.
I have no quarrel with {player}. I simply note that patience is cheaper than a seat on the council.

whisper.text: {player}, enjoy {fief} while it lasts. Favour in this council is borrowed, never owned.
Congratulations on {fief}. I trust you read the terms, because I certainly did before the vote.
A fief is a fine thing to hold, {player}. Holding it while the council watches is harder.
Do not mistake a grant for loyalty. Ruler's gifts come with strings, and I know whose hands hold them.
I would have voted differently on {fief}, but I suspect you already knew that. Mind your back.
{player}, I have no interest in a quarrel. I do hope you will remember who kept quiet during the vote.

global.text: {fief} has been granted to {player}. The council will judge what comes of it, as it judges everything.
Fresh grant of {fief} confirmed. Let us see whether its new holder can keep the walls standing through winter.
Ser {player} now holds {fief}. A reminder that a fief is a promise, and promises get audited.
Shall we see how {player} manages {fief} before drawing conclusions? Councils do like evidence.
The ruler's decree on {fief} is posted. Procedure was followed, which is more than can be said for last season.
Some will call the grant of {fief} a reward. I call it an invitation to be watched closely.

whisper.text: {player}, the grant of {fief} is settled. Now comes the harder part, keeping the other lords calm.
Holding {fief} means every council vote will affect you directly. Consider that before you speak.
I hear the ruler is pleased with your work on {fief}. Pleasure can be fickle, so keep records.
If you need a briefing on the councillors who matter, let me know. {fief} is not a simple place.
{fief} is yours now. I would suggest keeping your alliances loose until you know who owes whom.
Congratulations are in order, {player}, though I expect the fief's accounts will be less cheerful.

global.text: {fief} going to {player} is the council at its sensible best. Well chosen, and well earned.
A fine grant for someone who answers letters promptly. The council remembers such courtesy.
{player} now holds {fief}. I voted for it and I am not ashamed to say so in public.
Good news from the council chamber: {fief} has a new keeper, and I think the choice was wise.
People like {player} are the reason I still sit through long sessions. Enjoy {fief}, ser.
The ruler could not have picked better for {fief}. Our faction is proud to see it so placed.

whisper.text: {player}, I voted for {fief} to go to you. Do keep me in mind when the next seat opens.
Well done on {fief}. A friend in the council is worth more than any castle, so let us stay close.
I spoke for you in chamber today, {player}. A small debt, which I am sure you will remember.
{fief} suits you, {player}. Come to my table this week and we can plan how to keep it safe.
Let us meet before the next session, {player}. Holding {fief} needs allies, and I have a few to offer.
I hope {fief} brings you joy, {player}. Between us, I expect we will be dining out on this for months.

global.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction} at last. I shall reserve judgement until the council sees whether the oath holds.
Oaths are cheap in this realm, but {my_faction} keeps a long ledger. We shall see which column {player} lands in.
A new oath to {my_faction} has been recorded. Nobody on this council was consulted, which I find curious.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Do try to read the charter before the next vote. It is rather important here.
{player} joins our ranks with great ceremony. Ceremony does not win a seat, though. Ask anyone who lost one.
Good news for {my_faction}: another banner has been raised at our hall. I trust the newcomer knows where the doors are.

whisper.text: {player}, your oath is noted. So is the remark you made about the last council. We shall speak again once you have learned some manners.
You have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. A sensible choice, given the alternatives. Do not make me regret vouching for you.
A quiet word, {player}. Loyalty sworn under pressure rarely lasts. I will be watching the next vote closely.
{player}, I did not think you would kneel. Perhaps you will find my patience more useful than your pride.
Your oath arrived before your manners did, {player}. I shall keep both in my notes for the next council session.
Do not mistake a seat for a friendship, {player}. I have not forgotten who opposed the grant at the last sitting.

global.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. The council will decide what that means, as it always does.
Another oath recorded today. Whether it proves wise remains to be seen, and the council is in no hurry to decide.
Our ledger now lists {player} among our sworn members. Let us hope the fiefs they hold are as sound as their words.
Oaths are easily sworn and seldom kept, yet the council will still hold {player} to this one. We shall see.
{my_faction} accepts {player}'s oath. A reasonable step, though the true test comes at the next vote.
I note {player} has joined us quietly, without any fanfare. Perhaps that is how most useful alliances begin.

whisper.text: {player}, you have sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome. I would be glad to discuss how your interests and ours might align.
Congratulations on your oath, {player}. Now that you are one of us, we should discuss what a vote in council is worth to you.
A small matter, {player}. Your oath is recorded, but the council still wants to know where your loyalties truly sit.
{player}, I hope you chose us for good reasons. Ambition is welcome here, provided it is patient and properly argued.
Now that you have sworn, {player}, I may finally share a few things about the council that others have kept quiet.
You are sworn to {my_faction} now, {player}. Let us meet and see whether your ambitions and mine can sit at the same table.

global.text: {player} has joined {my_faction}, and I could not be more pleased. The council will remember who stood with us from the start.
Splendid news! {player} swears to {my_faction} and brings a fine reputation with them. Let the banners be raised.
With {player} sworn in, {my_faction} grows stronger. Ser, your place on the council is already being discussed.
Our ranks gain a capable new member today. {player} has chosen well, and I shall say so loudly at the next sitting.
{player} is now ours, and frankly the best recruit of the season. I shall toast the oath properly this evening.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Those who serve well here are rewarded, and I intend to see that you are.

whisper.text: {player}, I am delighted by your oath. Let us draft a plan for your first fief before the next council sits.
Well sworn, {player}. Between us we can see certain rivals removed from the council table by the next harvest.
You have made a wise choice, {player}. Stay close to me and I will ensure your name is heard in every chamber.
I hoped you would come to us, {player}. A person of your talents deserves a seat that others envy. Let me arrange it.
{player}, a quiet word of thanks. Your oath strengthens our position, and I do remember those who strengthen it.
Now that you are sworn, {player}, we should speak about recruiting a few sympathetic allies. I have names in mind.

global.text: {player} traded {my_faction}'s banner for another's. The council will hear every word of that transfer, I assure you.
Some people mistake a new banner for a new loyalty. {player} will learn the difference the hard way.
Ah, {player} has discovered that {faction} pays in promises. Do send word when the first one comes due.
A pity {player} could not hold a seat for even one season. Shall we start a ledger of the broken oaths?
Loyalty is cheap until it is priced. {player} has now shown us the price, and it was low.
We are not surprised. {player} always looked for the warmer hearth, and now we know where it is.

whisper.text: {player}, you left in the middle of a vote. Do not expect that absence to be forgotten in the next one.
I hope {faction} enjoys your company. They will discover quickly what the rest of us already knew.
You may tell yourself the move was strategic. I will simply note that it was public and very loud.
Every fief you once held still remembers your name. I am certain they will mention it at the next council.
A word of advice, {player}: turncloaks make poor allies and worse neighbours. Keep your gates barred.
When {faction} tires of you, and they will, the door back here may be shut. I would not count on it reopening.

global.text: {player} has moved to {faction}. Noted, filed, and set aside until we see whether the move was wise.
Curious timing, {player}. A new banner often arrives just before a new set of promises begins to fail.
The council minutes will record {player}'s departure in a single line. Everything else is still to be decided.
Lords come and go with the seasons. {player} may find {faction} colder than the hall they just left.
I make no judgement on {player}'s choice. Only its results, which will speak plainly enough soon.
Some will call it betrayal, others merely a change of weather. I prefer to wait and see which it proves to be.

whisper.text: {player}, I have no quarrel with your decision. I would simply like to know what {faction} offered you.
If you are still open to talk, I keep my correspondence clean. Write when your new seat grows uncomfortable.
Changing sides is your right, {player}. Just remember that every alliance here is only a loan on trust.
You will find {faction} keeps good records. Do make sure yours are in order before the next audit.
A quiet word: the council is still reviewing who stood where during the last levy. Your name is among them.
Whatever your reasons, {player}, I hope they hold up better than most promises made in this hall.

global.text: {player} may have walked away from {my_faction}, but I still hold the door open for capable allies.
Ambition is no crime, {player}. {my_faction} remembers those who served well and forgives the rest, eventually.
A tidy move to {faction}, {player}. When their council stumbles, I expect a clear-headed voice will be needed.
Whatever the reasons, {player}, the seat you left is not yet filled. Our table still values your judgment.
I bear no hard feelings. Politics is a long game, and I suspect you and I will sit across a table again.
Friends, the council should welcome back anyone who learns from a wrong turn. {player} may yet be among them.

whisper.text: {player}, no hard feelings from me. I still think you would do well on the council, wherever you sit.
Between us, I understand the pull of {faction}. Keep in touch, and I will tell you what is really being decided here.
Your old fief is still well kept, and I have made sure your name remains attached to its accounts.
If {faction} disappoints you, which I suspect it will, my door is open and the chairs are still warm.
Let us not let a banner come between friends. I would rather trade favours with you than chase you across the map.
You were a useful ally, {player}. Think of me as a backchannel whenever the politics turn dull or dangerous.

global.text: Burning {village} to the ground will look very poor in the council minutes, {player}. Someone should write that down.
The raid on {village} was bold. Pity the ashes will not win a single vote for whoever ordered it.
Ser {player} has discovered that fire is cheap and reputation is not. The council takes note.
Half of {village} is smoke now. I suppose that counts as a policy, if one has no interest in tax income.
Let it be recorded that {village} was burned while its garrison was away at a feast. Curious timing, is it not?
Every hearth in {village} is cold because someone wanted a headline. The council will not forget the cost.
Those who burn villages to earn a seat should first learn how seats are actually earned. Patience, {player}.
The fires at {village} lit the whole northern road. Plenty of lords saw who stood beside the torches.

whisper.text: {player}, you have made an enemy of my fief and a great many quiet friends in the council. Consider that a warning.
Burning {village} was a gift to me. The grain I lose is nothing next to the sympathy I will collect.
A word before you sleep easy, {player}: my people remember faces, and so do the magistrates who sit on the grant board.
I could have made this raid expensive for you in committee. Instead I shall simply let it be expensive in public.
You burned {village} and expect the council to thank you? Damn optimistic of you, {player}.
Shall we discuss terms, {player}? Restitution, a formal apology, and your name off the next levy list would be a fine start.
I have already written to three allies about {village}. By next session your name will be a question nobody wants answered.
Enjoy your victory at {village}, {player}. Victories like that have a way of ending in trials.

global.text: Raids on {village} will be discussed at the next session. Lords who wish to speak should prepare their evidence.
{village} burned last night. Nobody on the council has said who did it, which is either discretion or fear.
I have no quarrel with anyone yet, but the smoke over {village} is hard to ignore for those of us who pay the levy.
A village burned and a dozen questions asked. I expect answers before the next vote, not after.
It is a shame about {village}. Rebuilding costs coin, and coin has a way of finding its way to the council table.
Whoever set {village} alight should consider how the other fiefs will read it. Trust is slower to rebuild than walls.
The northern fiefs are talking about {village}. I would prefer they talk about trade instead, but here we are.
The council will hear the account of {village} properly. Nobody gets to decide the story before the evidence is in.

whisper.text: {player}, I am told {village} was hit. Was that a message, or merely an accident of enthusiasm?
No hard feelings yet, {player}. But I would like to know whether we are on the same side of the next vote.
I would rather not start a feud over {village}. Shall we meet and agree what the council is told?
The burning at {village} makes things awkward for both of us. A quiet conversation might save us embarrassment.
If you had a reason for {village}, I would be glad to hear it. Reasons can be worked with. Surprises cannot.
Tell me honestly, {player}, did you intend {village} to burn, or did the torches simply get ahead of you?
I am keeping an open mind about {village}. Convince me it was necessary and I will convince the others.
You and I have never fought over a grant, {player}. Let us keep it that way, shall we? Write to me first next time.

global.text: Renown is a fine thing, {player}, but it draws attention the council would rather not hand out so freely.
Everyone is talking about {player} now. Premature, I think, though I am sure the council will reach its own view in time.
A few rousing deeds and suddenly {player} fancies a seat in the council chamber. We shall see how long the applause lasts.
I have no quarrel with ambition, only with ambition that has not yet learned to wait its turn at the table.
Do enjoy the attention, {player}. Attention is a currency, and I suspect you will spend it faster than you earn it.
Strange how fame arrives so quickly for some. One does wonder who vouched for {player} before their name filled the boards.
{player} has been busy making a name for themselves. I will reserve judgement until that name survives a proper vote.
Several people have asked me about {player} this week. I told them I would wait for the minutes before forming an opinion.
Renown is never earned in a single afternoon, and the council keeps its own record of who is truly reliable, {player}.
Good for {player}, I suppose. Let us see whether the reputation survives the dull business of actually governing a fief.
Being talked about is not the same as being trusted. {player} is enjoying the first, and the second is still under review.
Odd how quickly a name travels once the right people start repeating it. I shall keep my notes on {player} for now.
The council should be proud to count {player} among its rising names. Anyone who answers the call this well deserves a seat.
Word of {player}'s deeds has reached every hall worth sitting in. I am glad to say I saw it coming.
{player} has shown that renown and sound judgement can share a cloak. I shall gladly speak for them when the votes are counted.
Anyone who doubts {player} is worth knowing is simply not paying attention. Those of us who are have been impressed for weeks.
A toast to {player}, whose reputation grows faster than most nobles would like. Find me afterwards, we should talk alliances.
Ser {player}, it is a pleasure to watch your name rise. Mind yourself, though. Rising names draw people who want to lean on them.
{fief} was mine until last week, and now {player} wears its banner. The council will hear every detail of how that happened.
Congratulations to {player} on taking {fief}. I trust the garrison will be paid from your own purse this time.
Walls change hands. Loyalties change faster. I merely note that {fief} has changed masters twice since spring.
A motion to review how {fief} was lost is being drafted. Those with nothing to hide should not fear it.
{player} took {fief} while its former steward was busy keeping this council honest. Convenient timing, wouldn't you say?
I will not gloat over {fief}. I will simply keep a ledger, and the ledger is long.

whisper.text: {player}, enjoy {fief} while the walls still stand. Fiefs are lent here, not given, and I keep the records.
You took {fief} from a table where I still had a chair. I am patient. Patience is how councils are won.
A small piece of advice: a captured town is a debt, not a trophy. Ask whoever held it before you how that went.
I could have made {fief} very uncomfortable for you. Instead I am choosing to be generous, which you may later regret.
Do not mistake a banner for a seat on the council, {player}. Votes are counted in rooms, not on walls.
Keep {fief} if you can hold it. The next vote on fief grants will be interesting, and I intend to attend.

global.text: {fief} has changed hands. Such things happen. The council will decide whether the transfer was lawful.
Some fiefs are won on the field, others at the negotiating table. I have no opinion on which {player} chose.
Was {fief} lost to strategy or to luck? Those who were there will tell the council, and I will listen carefully.
I have seen {fief} change banners before. The stones remain, and so does the paperwork.
Fiefs pass from hand to hand, and so do the grudges that come with them. We shall see which lasts longer here.
The council will hold its ordinary session on {fief}'s status. Attendance is expected, and so is patience.

whisper.text: {player}, no hard feelings about {fief}. Politics is politics, and today the scales tipped your way.
If you intend to keep {fief}, I suggest you speak to the council before someone else does it for you.
I am not angry about {fief}. I am taking notes, which is a habit I recommend to anyone new to our council.
We may have use for each other again, {player}. Holding a fief is expensive, and I know a few ways to share costs.
The garrison at {fief} is yours now, so I assume the upkeep is too. Do let me know if you need introductions.
Enjoy the view from {fief}'s walls. Views change quickly in this realm, as I am sure you have noticed.

global.text: A winning streak is a fine thing. Pity it has not yet bought a single seat on the council.
Every battle won is a debt owed somewhere. I do hope {player} keeps a ledger, because the bill will come due.
Remarkable run of victories. I wonder how many of the reports were written by the same tired clerk.
Some call this a golden age of conquest. Others call it a very expensive way to avoid a vote.
The council has noticed {player}'s wins. It has also noticed who pays for the lances and who doesn't.
Let the crowds cheer. Applause fades quickly, while those who hold the ledgers never forget.
A streak like that draws attention, and attention draws rivals. I suspect {player} enjoys the attention a little too much.
Winning every skirmish is impressive. Winning friends in the hall is a different sport entirely, and a harder one.

whisper.text: {player}, your little streak is charming. Do not mistake the council's applause for its trust. They are not the same.
I read the battle reports twice. Impressive, though a few of the names on the victory lists were quietly my own men.
Keep winning if you must. Every victory you post makes it easier for others to ask who is really paying for it.
The council discusses your campaigns more than your fief's harvest now. Be careful what that kind of attention costs you.
A word of caution, {player}. Those who win too often are soon asked to step aside, so you may want to rest.
Your record is admirable. Your alliances, however, are thin, and thin alliances snap the moment someone leans on them.
I would not be so pleased with the streak. Someone is already drafting the motion about its costs.
Enjoy the glory while it lasts, {player}. Glory is a poor shield against a unanimous vote in council.

global.text: Forty victories, or so the criers claim. Numbers grow in the telling, but the roads still need repairing.
Another win reported from the frontier. The council will debate it at length, as it does with everything.
{player} has been busy on the roads lately. Whether the realm benefits is a question for minutes, not for chat.
A long string of victories makes a good story. Stories cost nothing to tell, and the grain stores still cost a great deal.
Fine work on the frontier, I suppose. Let us see whether the fiefs hold once the banners are folded away.
Some are calling the recent campaigns decisive. I remain unconvinced until the tax rolls confirm it.
The streak continues. I will reserve judgement until someone explains what the realm gained beyond bragging rights.
Battles are won in the field, but the peace is negotiated in the hall. Wake me when the hall has something to say.

whisper.text: {player}, your recent campaigns have been noticed. I have no opinion yet, which in this council is a rare kindness.
I hear the battle tally is impressive. Send me the numbers if you like. I will read them with proper attention.
The streak is becoming tiresome to hear about, though I admit the ledgers look healthy for once. Good for you.
If you intend to seek a seat, the present momentum will help. Whether it helps enough is another matter entirely.
Your campaigns have drawn interest from several quarters. Nothing has been decided, and nothing needs to be yet, {player}.
Winning does not settle questions of rule. I say this as someone who has watched a few brilliant lords fall from favour.
A useful run, {player}. Keep it up and we may find time to discuss the matter of the vacant fief properly.
I have nothing against your victories. I simply prefer to see them written into a charter before I applaud.

global.text: {player} has carried more than their share of the frontier this season. I shall say so in the hall, loudly.
Forty victories in a row and still humble enough to read the council minutes. Rare, and we should encourage it.
A rousing streak from {player}. Every ballot in the hall will be easier to win with a record like that behind it.
Our banners are proud of {player}'s campaigns this season. Those who want a place beside us should take note.
{player} makes the realm look well-defended. I have already suggested to colleagues that a seat would suit them nicely.
Credit where it is due: {player}'s recent victories have done more for the roads than three motions in council.
Congratulations to {player} on another string of wins. Let it be recorded that the hall supports such ambition.
The realm sleeps easier with {player} on the frontier. I will gladly say as much to anyone who asks in council.

whisper.text: {player}, your streak has the hall buzzing. I have been defending your name over the last few votes, so you may thank me later.
I told two colleagues this morning that you are the most useful sword we have. Do not let it go to your head.
Keep up these victories and a council seat will find you without any further lobbying. I intend to make sure of it.
I backed your name for the next fief grant. A few more wins like these and the vote will be a formality.
You have made allies out of doubters this season, {player}. Let us talk properly about what you want in return.
Your campaigns look splendid in the minutes. Shall we meet quietly before the next session and arrange our votes?
Between us, the council already speaks of you as the next rising name in the hall. Best you are not caught unprepared.
Stay close to me, {player}. The people who matter have started asking about your name, and I know how to answer them.

global.text: Ser {player} let a prisoner walk free without a single coin in return. Bold, or simply careless? The council will want an explanation.
Some lords mistake mercy for strategy. A ransom would have paid for two levies. Now we have a grateful captive and an empty purse.
Letting a captive go unpaid is a fine way to lose friends at council, {player}. Mine will remember, and so will the treasury.
Curious how quickly the release was announced. Almost as if the timing was arranged to flatter someone's reputation for kindness.
A generous release, or a convenient one? Ransom money buys a great deal of loyalty. Shame to let it walk out the gate.
I do admire the gesture, truly. Pity gestures do not fill a treasury. Perhaps the next captive will be worth more to someone.
Freeing a prisoner for nothing sends a clear message to every noble watching. Kindness is cheap here, and so are the lords who show it.
Ser {player} has been generous with other people's ransoms. Tell me, what did the council gain from that? Nothing I can see.

whisper.text: {player}, a release without ransom is noted. I keep long records, and I will be pleasant about it when the time comes.
Your mercy cost the council a considerable sum. I trust you will be ready to explain that privately before the vote.
Do not mistake my silence for forgiveness. Freeing that captive was a choice, and choices here have consequences.
Interesting choice, releasing that captive for nothing. I would have priced the freedom, but then I am known for keeping accounts.
{player}, a word in confidence. Your generosity is admired in some quarters and questioned in mine. I suggest we discuss it soon.
You gave away a valuable prisoner for free, {player}. I am keeping a note of it, and the note is getting rather long.
Some lords learn from their mistakes. Others simply hand their captives back and hope nobody asks about the ransom. Guess which you are.
Enjoy your pleasant gesture while it lasts, {player}. Councils forget kindness quickly but never forget a missing treasury.

global.text: A prisoner walked free today without paying ransom. Few would do that, and fewer would bother explaining it.
It is worth noting that the release came without a ransom. The council may wish to discuss what that means for future captives.
Mercy is a fine virtue when it is documented. I trust the paperwork for today's release will be filed properly, in good time.
Some will call that kindness. I call it an unusual use of a valuable prisoner. Time will show which of us was right.
An unpaid release makes for good stories at court. Whether it makes for good politics remains to be seen, of course.
Word of the release has reached the council. Opinions vary, as they always do when someone else chooses the price of freedom.
I make no judgement on the release. The council will judge it soon enough, and the ledgers will tell the rest of the story.
A ransom refused is a message sent. I wonder who it was meant for, and whether the recipient has yet taken notice.

whisper.text: {player}, I heard about the release. A curious decision. I would appreciate a short account of your reasoning when convenient.
The captive is free and the purse is empty. I am not sure which of those you intended, but I am sure the council will ask.
I shall reserve judgement on your release until I hear the council's view. Do keep me informed of any further generosity.
Releasing a prisoner unransomed says a great deal about your priorities, {player}. I am still deciding what it says about you.
Pleasant day for it, {player}. Shall we speak about the release? Some of the other lords have asked me about it already.
No hard feelings about the ransom, {player}. I merely wish you had told the council first. Procedure exists for a reason.
Your release of that captive will be discussed at the next session. Come prepared, and perhaps with a clearer account.
I am not offended by your generosity, {player}. I am simply counting. Someone at court must, and it may as well be me.

global.text: Ser {player} showed mercy where others would have haggled. The council should take note of lords who value people over coin.
A gracious release, and not a single coin demanded. That is the sort of conduct this realm should be building its reputation on.
Three cheers for {player}, who freed a captive without a ransom. Such restraint is rare, and the council values rare things.
Kindness rarely fills a treasury, but it fills a hall full of allies. {player} has just gained several admirers at court.
Well done to {player} for the unpaid release. I have already begun drafting a motion praising such principled leadership.
The release was handled with real grace. Some lords count only gold. I am glad we have one who counts favours as well.
{player} let a prisoner go with no ransom attached. Whatever the treasurer says, that will be remembered well in council.
Generosity like that does not go unnoticed here. Expect a few invitations to discuss matters of influence over the coming weeks.

whisper.text: {player}, that release was beautifully done. I have friends on the council who will hear about it, and they will be impressed.
You released that captive without ransom, and I could not be prouder to call you an ally. Let us dine and discuss what comes next.
I will speak for you at the next council session. A lord who frees prisoners for nothing deserves a seat at the table.
Your mercy has done more for your standing than any ransom could. Keep it up, and I will see you receive the credit it deserves.
Splendid choice, {player}. Gold spent on a grudge is gold wasted. Shall we talk about where your support might do the most good?
I put your name forward for the council's mercy committee, and the motion passed easily. Your release helped more than you know.
Do not let the treasurer's complaints trouble you. The release was principled, and principled lords are hard to find these days.
Between us, the release was the wisest thing I have heard all week. Come find me before the next session and we will plan the rest.

global.text: Council convenes at dawn, and I expect every banner at the table. Absence will be noted in the minutes, naturally.
Let us be clear: {enemy_faction} chose this war, and the ledgers will show who paid for it first.
A war nobody can afford is only a rumour with swords. Let us see how long {enemy_faction} keeps its coffers full.
Peace is a fine word, though I doubt {enemy_faction} has ever learned to spell it. I remain willing to draft terms.
Some lords will sharpen their blades tonight. I prefer to sharpen arguments, which last considerably longer.
Ser, do not mistake my patience for weakness. {my_faction} sends its regards and a very long list of grievances.
Funny how every grievance we raised in council suddenly became a banner. History is kind to whoever drafts it.
A quiet word to the sensible lords: the border fiefs will change hands soon, and I would rather it happen by treaty.

whisper.text: {player}, I'll be brief. {enemy_faction} threatens us both, and a sensible lord would not wait to be picked off.
Nothing binding yet, {player}. Only a conversation about whether {enemy_faction} should keep its current borders.
I don't trust easily, {player}, so I'll keep this simple. Help me contain {enemy_faction} and I'll keep my word.
Consider this a courtesy, {player}. {enemy_faction} has begun courting the council, and I doubt you'd enjoy the result.
We have no history to speak of, {player}, which may be an advantage. A quiet pact against {enemy_faction} could suit us both.
Think it over before answering, {player}. The council meets soon, and I would prefer to have an ally in that chamber.
I have no quarrel with you, {player}. I do have one with {enemy_faction}, and a neutral party's silence would be noted.
Let us be practical, {player}. {enemy_faction} profits from our disunity. Shall we discuss terms by letter?
Ser {player}, you have always been the sensible one. I'd like us to stand together against {enemy_faction} before the vote.
Between friends, {player}: {enemy_faction} is quietly buying the seats we both depend on. Shall we stop them together?
I think of you as an ally already, {player}. Let us put that on paper and aim it squarely at {enemy_faction}.
A small thing, {player}. {rival} speaks of you rather unkindly. Pair with me against {enemy_faction} and we'll have the final word.
Keep this between us, {player}. Your fief grant is safe with me, and I would like {enemy_faction} to lose theirs.
We make a fine pair in council, {player}. Let's show {enemy_faction} what unity looks like before they show us.
Come by the hall when you can, {player}. I have a plan against {enemy_faction} and I'd rather build it with a friend.
Honestly, {player}, I'm tired of watching {enemy_faction} smile at the council. Shall we wipe that smile away together?
{player}, I will be direct, which I rarely am. {fief} is under siege in all but name, and the council dithers.
Ser {player}, {enemy_faction} has been pressing our border towns. Any help you offered would be remembered in council.
I am told you have spare men. {fief} could use them, and I would hate for the credit to go to someone else.
Wars are rarely lost on the field, {player}. They are lost in committee, while everyone waits for someone else to act.
Another emergency at {fief}. I am tired of writing letters, {player}. Perhaps you would prefer to sign one for once?
Those who sit out a crisis at {fief} tend to find their seats reassigned afterwards. Consider where you stand, {player}.
{fief} is on fire and the council is arguing about the colour of the smoke. Care to lend a bucket, {player}?
I have the votes to save {fief}, but not the margin to spare. Would you add your name to the motion, {player}?
{player}, you have always been reasonable. {fief} is in trouble and I would rather trust a friend than a committee.
Between us, {player}, I need your swords at {fief} before the next council sits. Name your price and we shall discuss it.
Our last vote together was rather productive, wasn't it? {fief} now needs the same spirit, {player}.
I shall keep this brief. {fief} is slipping, and I trust you more than anyone else on the roll. Will you ride out?
Forgive the hour, {player}. {enemy_faction} has taken two villages and my allies are wavering. I need you steady.
If {fief} falls, I shall blame the weather, the messengers, and the treasurer. Fortunately, you are none of those, {player}.
Certain people in council would love to see {fief} fall on their watch. Let us make sure they are disappointed, {player}.
Friendship is tested when a fief is burning, {player}. I like to think ours has survived worse. Could you help?
Ser {player}, the council has grown tired of our quarrel, so I propose we settle it on the field outside {village} at dusk.
You have spent a whole season whispering about my fief. Come to {town}'s eastern road and say it to my face with steel in hand.
Your votes have been tallied and found wanting, {player}. Let us see whether your sword is any more persuasive than your speeches.
Another motion, another grudge. Honestly, {player}, I am tired of it too. Meet me at {village} and let us end this properly.
Power is merely the sum of who is willing to bleed for it. Let us discover which of us that is at {town}'s old mill.
Enough petitions. Meet me at the ford below {town} and let steel settle what your speeches never could, {player}.
You have my word I will not bring a banner. The scribes are still sulking about the last one. Come to {village} at dawn.
I have sent my intentions to the council in writing. Now I ask you to meet me on the field at {village}, where words count for less.
Ser {player}, no offence intended, but our fiefs share a border and a disagreement is due. Shall we meet at {village}?
I have no quarrel with you yet, {player}. Still, a formal challenge at {town} would be the honourable way to test our standing.
Let us be candid. Neither of us will yield an acre without a contest. A friendly bout near {village} may spare the council a vote.
Some matters are better settled by steel than by ballot. Would you join me at {village} for a sparring match, {player}?
The council will ask who holds the better claim. I would rather answer that on a field near {town} than in another dull session.
Ser {player}, I suspect we both tire of arguing in committee. Name a day and a meadow, and we shall see who is truly in earnest.
Should our differences persist, I would prefer a clean contest to whispers in the hall. Are you willing to meet at {village}?
No insult is meant, {player}. Yet a duel of honour would settle the question of the {town} grant better than another motion.
{player}, the council minutes are already drafted, and your name appears nowhere in them. Such a pity, truly.
Your motion failed by three votes, {player}. I counted them myself, because someone in this realm must keep proper records.
I had hoped you would be easier to work with by now. Perhaps the next season will be kinder to us both.
Every alliance has a weakest member, {player}. I have been reading yours very carefully, and I am not impressed.
{rival} mentioned, in the kindest possible way, that you are overrated. I thought you deserved to hear it from a friend.
You walk into council like a fox who forgot the henhouse is locked. Charming, truly, though the hens have noticed.
Power is patient, {player}. Those who mistake my courtesy for weakness tend to learn the difference rather late.
I do wish you would stop trying so damn hard, {player}. It has become embarrassing for everyone at the table.
